rv.q: The show casts a shimmering, softly enrapturing spell; it’s fragrant with its own perfume, a mixture of melody, memory and affection.

As its actresses weave through that hanging garden, they look ravishing in Toni-Leslie James’s svelte period dresses — and so does this small-scale musical, whose tribute to women’s sacrifices and encouragement is put in their own finest light.
It’s got so much going for it but dodges away from total commitment.
Indeed, all kinds of enchantment are at work in this production...
“The Gardens of Anuncia” is arguably LaChiusa’s finest musical, because it is also deceptively his most simple.
It’s an evocative feat of design: moving, gorgeous, and practical at once.

“ ‘The Gardens of Anuncia’ is a delicate work that is dependent on its perfect cast and the sure eye of its director to keep things gently flowing. There is no room for rough spots or prima donnas anywhere along the way.
Their result arrives as a labor of love.

Daniele has crafted a simple, gorgeous production, helped by an elegant garden trellis-like backdrop, designed by Mark Wendland, which seems to shift and reshape under Jules Fisher and Peggy Eisenhauer’s ethereal lighting as we progress through Anuncia’s memories.
Anuncia and her loved ones are a delight to be around, and Lopez and company remain a collective wonder.

It’s a deliberately modest musical in many ways. The scenic design is simple… There is little plot. There isn’t even much dancing… I also can’t claim that any of the 14 songs in “The Gardens of Anuncia” are an earworm like, say, “Don’t Cry For Me Argentina.”
With a little more cultivation, these “Gardens” could blossom into a theatrical staple that will have many a regional production – or maybe become a show truly worthy of a future Broadway production.
A sweet lovely chamber show, it is also tepid and tame and has little impact.
While the vignettes of Anuncia’s childhood are heartfelt, the framing of Tía’s burial and Anuncia’s awards ceremony lacks impact and lags.
Both have their satisfactions but ultimately leave you wanting more than their approximately 90-minute running times provide.
The show is crisp and rarely dull; however, if it ever moves on from here one hopes it will offer a better representation of why we care so much about Graciela Daniele’s artistry to begin with.
It’s a nice tribute to the women who raised her, but does that make good drama? In this case, not quite.
The Gardens of Anuncia is a captivating chamber musical that straddles the line between modesty and maximalism, stubbornly defying both categorization and commercial impulses.
“The Gardens of Anuncia” is a small warm production set on a nearly bare stage at the Mitzi E. Newhouse.

Sensitively directed by Daniele, it offers one not only a glimpse of the icon before she became famous for her choreography but a portrait of the artist as a mature woman, looking back on her star-dusted life.
If only there had been more fantasy to augment this lovely bio-musical and lift it airborne.
The Gardens of Anuncia charms as a memory musical that is also a carefully crafted flower seeded well from a strong friendship.

cn.t: LaChiusa's delicate memory musical about choreographer Graciela Daniele's Argentine childhood earns praise for its gorgeous score and stellar female cast, though some critics find the fragmented structure dramatically slight and wanting more substance.
